note: Every hash, head and canonical byte string in this file was produced by the PYTHON reference implementation. The JavaScript side must reproduce them EXACTLY. This file is the receipt.
i_json_note: I-JSON BOUNDARY, FOUND WHILE CROSS-CHECKING THESE TWO IMPLEMENTATIONS. An integer above 2^53 (9007199254740993) is NOT an I-JSON value, so RFC 8785 does not say how to serialize it -- and the two languages DISAGREE: Python's json keeps the exact integer through a round trip, while JSON.parse in JavaScript cannot represent it and rounds it to 9007199254740992. A body containing such an integer would therefore be hashed DIFFERENTLY by the two implementations, with no spec to say which is right. The fix is not to pick a side: a chain whose body leaves the I-JSON range must be REFUSED, not silently canonicalized. The case below therefore uses 2^53 exactly, which is inside the range and survives both languages unchanged.
digest_recipe: sha256 over, for each case in order: the head, a newline, then each canonical body with a newline. Computed identically in Python and JavaScript -- it is a digest of the SEMANTIC content, not of this file's bytes, so it does not depend on how either language happens to format a float.
